features.name: M0.1 Environment and application skeleton
features.behavior: A fresh checkout installs with `uv sync` and runs the test suite with no API keys and no network. A FastAPI app factory serves GET /health/live -> 200 {status: ok} and GET /health/ready -> 200 with a dependency status map (no dependencies yet). Settings load from environment with LLM_MODE=mock and ENABLE_LIVE_LLM=false as defaults; .env.example matches handoff section 6. Logs are structured JSON and never print environment values. Ruff, mypy (strict, apps/ and packages/) and pytest with markers integration/live are configured in pyproject.toml; package.json lint/typecheck/test scripts chain the uv commands; CI installs uv and runs npm run check without secrets. Requirements: FR-001 (partial: health), NFR-009, NFR-010.
features.verification: Acceptance tests hit both health endpoints through the app factory; a test asserts LLM_MODE defaults to mock; a socket-blocking fixture proves no outbound network during tests. Report exact uv, Python and package versions in the session note.

features.name: M0.2 Synthetic data and persistence
features.behavior: docker compose starts PostgreSQL with pgvector and a healthcheck. Migrations create tenants, users, roles, business_sales, documents and document_chunks with tenant scope and stable ids/hashes for citations. A deterministic seed loads two synthetic tenants (demo-a, demo-b) and local fixture documents. Analytics run through a read-only database role and an ACL-restricted query function. Requirements: FR-003 (data side), FR-004, NFR-010.
features.verification: Integration tests: seeded queries return the expected synthetic totals; tenant demo-a cannot read any demo-b row or document; an INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP through the read-only role is rejected by Postgres privileges.

features.name: M1.1 Model provider port and mock
features.behavior: packages/core defines ModelRequest/ModelResponse and an LLMProvider protocol with generate() and capabilities(). MockLLMProvider returns deterministic fixture responses keyed by test case. A typed capability registry rejects unsupported model capabilities before execution with MODEL_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. LiteLLMProvider in packages/llm normalizes tool calls, structured output, usage fields and errors (RATE_LIMITED, AUTH_FAILED, TIMEOUT, CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, BUDGET_EXCEEDED) and is never selected unless LLM_MODE and ENABLE_LIVE_LLM opt in. Requirements: FR-009, FR-010, NFR-009.
features.verification: A shared contract suite runs against the mock and a stubbed LiteLLM adapter; capability rejection happens before any provider call; the test run proves no provider network access.

features.name: M1.2 First vertical-slice graph
features.behavior: One LangGraph workflow (6-8 nodes, typed AgentRunState, bounded steps, calls, time and context budget) takes the sample task, calls a typed read-only sales tool and a permission-filtered retrieval tool, and returns a schema-valid report whose claims cite source ids. features.verification: Deterministic end-to-end run in mock mode reproduces the expected metrics and citations (recorded as a replay fixture); abstention and policy-rejection cases pass; budget exhaustion ends in an explicit terminal status.

features.name: M2.1 MCP server and policy gateway
features.behavior: A first-party MCP server exposes get_sales_summary, search_approved_documents and get_issue_details (read) and create_followup_ticket (sandbox write) with JSON-schema contracts. A separate server-side tool gateway enforces allowlist, principal/tenant scope, argument validation and a policy decision log. Writes need an approval bound to principal, action-payload hash, policy version, expiry and run. Requirements: FR-005, FR-006, NFR-001, NFR-002.
features.verification: A benign approved write commits one sandbox ticket; denied, expired, mutated and replayed approvals and malicious model tool calls (including crafted tenant args and prompt-injected documents) are rejected with no write; every decision is logged.

features.name: M2.2 Idempotency and fault recovery
features.behavior: Runs checkpoint to Postgres and resume after process restart with the same thread_id. A tool_executions registry with UNIQUE (tenant_id, tool_name, idempotency_key) reserves and claims each write atomically through reserved -> executing -> succeeded/failed/uncertain; uncertain outcomes reconcile by deterministic external reference before any retry. The docs state this is not a universal exactly-once guarantee. Requirements: FR-007, FR-008, NFR-003.
features.verification: Concurrent retries of the same approved action create exactly one sandbox ticket; an injected crash after external commit but before acknowledgment restarts into one recorded operation; an ambiguous result is reconciled; HITL approval survives an API restart.

features.name: M3.1 Observability, security evaluation and feedback
features.behavior: OpenTelemetry spans follow the spec taxonomy with optional Langfuse export that needs no key in tests; secrets and PII are redacted before export. features.name: M4.1 Three-specialist comparison
features.behavior: Research, Data Analyst and Reporting roles are introduced as subgraphs only after the single-workflow baseline is measured, and both run on the same golden dataset. A benchmark report compares task success, citation accuracy, tool calls, tokens, latency and cost with dataset, model, sample size and limitations. The simpler orchestration is kept unless the specialists measurably win. Requirements: FR-016, NFR-006, NFR-008.
features.verification: The comparison runs reproducibly in mock mode and writes a versioned results file; any hosted-model numbers come from an explicitly opted-in, budget-capped live run and are labeled as such.

features.name: Phase 2: tenant-isolated run checkpoints
features.behavior: Checkpoint thread ids carry the tenant (<tenant>/thread-<run_id>). Row-level security on LangGraph's checkpoint tables limits every read and write to the tenant set for the checkpointer's connection; a connection without a tenant sees and writes nothing. A checkpointer scoped to one tenant cannot read, resume or overwrite another tenant's run. Requirements: NFR-001, FR-008 (D-010 risk).
features.verification: Integration tests: a paused demo-a run is invisible to and cannot be resumed by a demo-b-scoped checkpointer; an unscoped app-login session sees zero checkpoint rows; writing a checkpoint row for another tenant's thread is rejected; the existing approval pause/resume still works with tenant-scoped checkpointers.

features.name: Phase 2: HTTP approvals and run resume
features.behavior: POST /v1/runs accepts propose_followup and returns awaiting_approval with the bound proposal; API runs are checkpointed per tenant. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/approvals/{approval_id} with decision approve|reject records the decision through the gateway for the demo user and resumes the run, which writes at most one ticket. GET /v1/runs/{run_id} returns the run's current sanitized detail from its checkpoint. Gateway refusals map to problem details (404 unknown, 403 other principal or run, 409 already decided or used); another tenant's run is not found. Requirements: FR-001, FR-006, FR-013.
features.verification: Integration tests over HTTP: propose, approve, resume writes one ticket; reject completes without a ticket; a second decision is 409 with no second ticket; another demo user gets 403; another tenant gets 404 for GET and approval; GET shows awaiting_approval then completed; resume makes no model call.

features.name: Phase 2: hosted-model live run
features.behavior: The Gemini Flash-Lite hosted model (gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite) is registered in the deny-by-default capability registry with its real capabilities, and its key is read from GEMINI_API_KEY. The live provider is selected only with LLM_MODE plus ENABLE_LIVE_LLM=true, and a hard per-run cost budget (LLM_BUDGET_USD) aborts the run with BUDGET_EXCEEDED before the LiteLLM-reported spend crosses it. The eval corpus and benchmark run once live, explicitly opted-in and budget-capped, and their results record dataset_version, git_sha, model, prompt_version and actual spend. Requirements: FR-009, FR-010, NFR-009.
features.verification: Acceptance tests run against a stubbed LiteLLM adapter with no network: the Gemini Flash-Lite model is registered and selected only on opt-in; a run whose stubbed spend would cross LLM_BUDGET_USD aborts with BUDGET_EXCEEDED before the provider call; GEMINI_API_KEY is read from the environment and never emitted in logs or errors. The owner-opted live corpus and benchmark run is documented as a manual step, not CI.

features.name: Phase 2: retrieval relevance baseline
features.behavior: A versioned synthetic retrieval query set measures the existing permission-filtered HashingEmbedder/pgvector search without changing ranking. The benchmark records per-query retrieved chunk ids, Recall@k and reciprocal rank for answerable queries, labels queries with no accessible relevant evidence separately, and reports any forbidden-document hit. JSON records dataset version, dataset hash, supplied git SHA, embedding model and aggregate Recall@k/MRR. It performs no model calls and uses the read-only analytics role. Requirements: FR-003, NFR-007, NFR-010.
features.verification: Offline metric/schema/CLI tests and local PostgreSQL acceptance tests verify metric denominators, no-relevant-evidence handling, tenant/role filtering and reproducible results. Run the versioned corpus once and record actual measured results, with no unmeasured quality threshold.
